A-stationary-canon.cadence: R-CPB-14, OFF — A2d's stationary FORMULA at the shipped rate. A2d's cadence was STATISTICALLY STATIONARY — 17 births every revolution forever, so ~7.7 cuts alive at every instant and every second looking like every other one. The births are organised into EPOCHS: a sequence of 5..13 cuts runs at the ruled 17/rev rate, ENDS, and BEGINS AGAIN after a seeded gap of 0.10..0.40 rev. Mean period 0.779 rev, mean density 11.55 cuts/rev, duty 68%. THE GAP IS THE ANGULAR RE-ANCHOR: a cut is a mark left where the steel was, so its bearing is `a0 + TAU * birth` and is not a free parameter — the only honest way to make a sequence begin again somewhere else on the circle is to make it begin again at a different TIME. Adding an angle offset would draw burn marks the hammer never passed through. Epoch length and gap are pure functions of (CUT_SEED=20260813, epoch index); the per-cut hashes GAIN the epoch index and change in no other way. THE MAX GAP IS SET AGAINST THE PERSISTENCE, not by eye — and the silence is NOT the gap: the last birth of a sequence sits half a bin before it ends and the first birth of the next half a bin after it starts, so silence = gap + (1 + jitter)/rate = 0.40 + 0.0912 = 0.4912 rev against a 0.45 rev life, leaving the ring fully dark for at most 0.0412 rev = 0.0148 s = 0.44 of a 30 fps frame at the very worst draw the seed can produce. The first derivation of this bound read the silence as the gap alone, typed 0.52, and left a TWO-FRAME blackout that the falsification row measured off the rendered window. Undulation, not a strobe. ⚑ AND THE RATE IS THE RESTORED ONE (R-CPB-15): Matt pulled the density lever A2e's landing named, so this cadence aims its realized MEAN at the RATIFIED 11.0 cuts/rev (band +/-0.5) rather than at its own rate — the analytic mean above is 11.547 — and raising the rate shrank the blackout bound as a SIDE EFFECT, because narrower bins mean less slack at each end of a sequence.

pattern.alternation: STRICT on the global stroke index g = rev * 17 + slot: g even is SWORD, g odd is CLAW. The ruling alternates the CLASSES and randomises the INTERVALS, not the other way round. With 17 births per revolution — an odd number — the parity at a given slot flips every revolution, so in the STATIONARY cadence the same bearing takes the other class next time round. A cut's bearing is a0 + TAU * birth, so the integer revolution contributes a whole turn and drops out: an EVEN rate would repeat class-at-bearing every 0.36 s, which is why the rate raise landed on an odd integer rather than on the one that centred the mean better. The UNDULATING cadence is parity-independent — its g runs continuously across epochs of varying length, so nothing about it turns on this.
pattern.determinism: R-CPB-12 clause 5 / GL-18 / FG-10. Every interval, class, height, variant and per-finger stagger is a HASH of (CUT_SEED=20260813, revolution index, slot index) — the same `_hash2` the spark schedule has used since A2b. There is no `randi()` anywhere in this file, seeded or otherwise, no RNG object, no wall clock and no per-frame accumulation. The same tick produces the same frame across process restarts AND across two fresh builds, and the motion smoke asserts both.
pattern.palette: ONE RAMP, FOUR CONSUMERS (R-CPB-13): white-hot (1.00, 0.97, 0.90) -> orange (1.00, 0.42, 0.06) -> RED (0.98, 0.07, 0.02), knee at 0.56 of the DECAYED age axis (= 0.3485 of a linear life, derived), gamma 0.55 BELOW 1 so the energy drops fast off the steel and then CRAWLS — the crawl is where the red lives. CONSUMERS: the SWORD cuts and the CLAW cuts (one shader, one pool, the stops written onto every material), the SPARK contact bursts and the EMBER garnish (the ramp SAMPLED at 32 stops onto their Gradients — they do not copy the numbers, they evaluate the function). pattern.undulation: R-CPB-14, OFF — A2d's stationary FORMULA at the shipped rate. A2d's cadence was STATISTICALLY STATIONARY — 17 births every revolution forever, so ~7.7 cuts alive at every instant and every second looking like every other one. The births are organised into EPOCHS: a sequence of 5..13 cuts runs at the ruled 17/rev rate, ENDS, and BEGINS AGAIN after a seeded gap of 0.10..0.40 rev. Mean period 0.779 rev, mean density 11.55 cuts/rev, duty 68%. THE GAP IS THE ANGULAR RE-ANCHOR: a cut is a mark left where the steel was, so its bearing is `a0 + TAU * birth` and is not a free parameter — the only honest way to make a sequence begin again somewhere else on the circle is to make it begin again at a different TIME. Adding an angle offset would draw burn marks the hammer never passed through. Epoch length and gap are pure functions of (CUT_SEED=20260813, epoch index); the per-cut hashes GAIN the epoch index and change in no other way. THE MAX GAP IS SET AGAINST THE PERSISTENCE, not by eye — and the silence is NOT the gap: the last birth of a sequence sits half a bin before it ends and the first birth of the next half a bin after it starts, so silence = gap + (1 + jitter)/rate = 0.40 + 0.0912 = 0.4912 rev against a 0.45 rev life, leaving the ring fully dark for at most 0.0412 rev = 0.0148 s = 0.44 of a 30 fps frame at the very worst draw the seed can produce. The first derivation of this bound read the silence as the gap alone, typed 0.52, and left a TWO-FRAME blackout that the falsification row measured off the rendered window. Undulation, not a strobe. ⚑ AND THE RATE IS THE RESTORED ONE (R-CPB-15): Matt pulled the density lever A2e's landing named, so this cadence aims its realized MEAN at the RATIFIED 11.0 cuts/rev (band +/-0.5) rather than at its own rate — the analytic mean above is 11.547 — and raising the rate shrank the blackout bound as a SIDE EFFECT, because narrower bins mean less slack at each end of a sequence.

A2c's ring was parented to the spinning holder, which is exactly equivalent for a full circle and exactly WRONG for a discrete pattern: a burn mark stays where the steel touched.

elbows.measure_basis: R-CPB-11-B. The elbow apex's displacement off the SHOULDER-TO-WRIST line, decomposed onto the CHEST's own axes (the shoulder line, measured — not the pelvis's, which this coiled torso is 38 deg out of). OUT is away from the midline for BOTH arms, so one bar covers both and an INWARD elbow reads negative. A2c measured OUT +0.0172 / -0.0109 m against DOWN +0.1031 / +0.0513 — forty degrees of right-elbow flexion pointing along the arm's own visual axis, which is why Matt read straight arms off a joint angle that said otherwise. A BEND IS A DIRECTION, NOT A SCALAR.

occlusion.basis: R-CPB-11-C, GEOMETRIC. (a) arm vs arm: the minimum distance between the two arms' SKINNED vertex sets, 687 x 687 verts, in body space. (b) hand vs haft: for every skinned hand vertex, the PARITY of the crossings of a radially-outward ray against the weapon's own 36 triangles in the fists' band — odd means the vertex is INSIDE THE STEEL, AND whether that vertex's own skinned normal faces radially OUTWARD, which is what makes the burial visible. Exact, not an envelope: a max-radius-per-bin envelope calls this hammer's talon pommel a cylinder and condemns a fist that is nowhere near it. The envelope clearance is reported beside the boolean as the continuous number to tune against, and it is the number that may be negative while the law still holds.

pose.oscillation: NOT BUILT, and that is a choice with a reason. A per-revolution wobble would be a second clock beside the trace's (GL-18) and would make the spark radius time-varying, which weakens the one law the ring is built on — sparks at EXACTLY the hammer's reach. Cheap to add later as a pure function of the same tick; veto-open.

stance.basis: R-CPB-8. The boots are PLANTED at measured floor points and the legs are SOLVED to them (law of cosines, knee poled along that boot's own toes so the apex LEADS). A2b-r rotated each shin about `side` — the SWING's lateral axis, not the leg's — by a NEGATIVE angle, which decomposed into hyperextension (-15.3 deg about body-left) AND a sideways break out of the thigh's plane (-21.0 deg about body-forward): both halves of Matt's 'bending backwards (inwards)' from one wrong axis. PRESENTATION CHOICE, NO WIRE BASIS.
stance.bone_line_basis: RETIRED (R-CPB-11-A), kept visible. The ankle-to-toe BONE line and the foot bone's basis against its rest basis. Correct arithmetic on the wrong object: this rig's bone line is horizontal at bind and its boot underside is raked 18.1 deg against it, so levelling the line reproduces the rake. Reads 0.000 deg on the DEFECTIVE pose and 18.14 deg on the CORRECT one. The live flatness read is `stance.sole` (measure_soles).
stance.hip_drop_basis: BISECTED, not typed: the smallest pelvis drop at which the deeper knee reaches KNEE_BEND_DEG=26 deg with BOTH boots on the floor, solved against the rig's own bone lengths. A 15.0 deg split plants the boots 0.2009 m off the spin line each, which is further from the hips than the legs are long — so the drop is compulsory arithmetic before it is anybody's taste.
stance.measure_basis: bone globals composed from LOCAL poses (NOT get_bone_global_pose, which reads a cache a headless harness never refreshes, and NOT an AABB, which is the bind-pose box and cannot see a pose at all — the instrument that one replaced scored 0.0000 m of ground gap for a boot 0.094 m in the air). knee_apex_fwd is the knee's break off the hip-ankle line projected on that boot's OWN toe direction: positive leads, negative is the hyperextension Matt named. FLATNESS IS NOT MEASURED HERE ANY MORE — see stance.sole.

sole.measure_basis: R-CPB-11-A. THE BOOT'S UNDERSIDE PROFILE — a side-elevation silhouette, computed. The skin is evaluated on the CPU (vertex' = sum_j w_j * (bone_pose(bind_j) * bind_pose_j) * v, composed from LOCAL bone poses, so no frame and no cache is needed); the sole SET is decided ONCE at rest — the boot's underside from the heel contact forward, within 0.006 m of each station's own floor — and those same vertices by KEY are what every pose is judged on. `sole_pitch_deg` is the least-squares slope of the lowest surface across 10 stations heel-to-toe: POSITIVE IS TOES UP, the defect Matt named, and it reads +18.1 on the A2c article. Roll is measured across the HEEL only, the one part of this boot with real lateral width. THREE EARLIER INSTRUMENTS SCORED THIS POSE FLAT: the ankle-to-toe BONE line (A2c, 0.000 deg), a lowest-22-mm vertex band (0.000 deg — on a raked boot it selects the heel pad alone), and down-facing skinned FACES (which on this asset are four 2 cm facets under the ankle, because the real underside triangle wraps up the point and its normal is 64 deg off vertical).

stance.sole_basis: R-CPB-11-A. The boot's whole UNDERSIDE is raked NOSE-UP in the bind pose — one ramp from a heel edge at y = -0.0177 to a raised point at y = +0.0114 over 0.0868 m, 18.1 deg — while the ankle-to-toe BONE line is horizontal. So A2c's 'level the foot to its rest basis' levelled the bone line to 0.000 deg AND faithfully reproduced the mesh's rake. The ankle's orientation and its height are now SOLVED against the rendered underside: 5 laps of {plant -> bisect the drop -> solve both legs -> level the foot -> MEASURE THE MESH -> correct pitch, roll and lift}. The knee target is re-bisected INSIDE every lap, so the ratified knees survive the foot fix instead of being spent on it.

pattern.alternation: STRICT on the global stroke index g = rev * 17 + slot: g even is SWORD, g odd is CLAW. The ruling alternates the CLASSES and randomises the INTERVALS, not the other way round. With 17 births per revolution — an odd number — the parity at a given slot flips every revolution, so in the STATIONARY cadence the same bearing takes the other class next time round. A cut's bearing is a0 + TAU * birth, so the integer revolution contributes a whole turn and drops out: an EVEN rate would repeat class-at-bearing every 0.36 s, which is why the rate raise landed on an odd integer rather than on the one that centred the mean better. The UNDULATING cadence is parity-independent — its g runs continuously across epochs of varying length, so nothing about it turns on this.
pattern.determinism: R-CPB-12 clause 5 / GL-18 / FG-10. Every interval, class, height, variant and per-finger stagger is a HASH of (CUT_SEED=20260813, revolution index, slot index) — the same `_hash2` the spark schedule has used since A2b. There is no `randi()` anywhere in this file, seeded or otherwise, no RNG object, no wall clock and no per-frame accumulation. The same tick produces the same frame across process restarts AND across two fresh builds, and the motion smoke asserts both.
pattern.palette: ONE RAMP, FOUR CONSUMERS (R-CPB-13): white-hot (1.00, 0.97, 0.90) -> orange (1.00, 0.42, 0.06) -> RED (0.98, 0.07, 0.02), knee at 0.56 of the DECAYED age axis (= 0.3485 of a linear life, derived), gamma 0.55 BELOW 1 so the energy drops fast off the steel and then CRAWLS — the crawl is where the red lives. CONSUMERS: the SWORD cuts and the CLAW cuts (one shader, one pool, the stops written onto every material), the SPARK contact bursts and the EMBER garnish (the ramp SAMPLED at 32 stops onto their Gradients — they do not copy the numbers, they evaluate the function). pattern.undulation: R-CPB-14, ON. A2d's cadence was STATISTICALLY STATIONARY — 17 births every revolution forever, so ~7.7 cuts alive at every instant and every second looking like every other one. The births are organised into EPOCHS: a sequence of 5..13 cuts runs at the ruled 17/rev rate, ENDS, and BEGINS AGAIN after a seeded gap of 0.10..0.40 rev. Mean period 0.779 rev, mean density 11.55 cuts/rev, duty 68%. THE GAP IS THE ANGULAR RE-ANCHOR: a cut is a mark left where the steel was, so its bearing is `a0 + TAU * birth` and is not a free parameter — the only honest way to make a sequence begin again somewhere else on the circle is to make it begin again at a different TIME. Adding an angle offset would draw burn marks the hammer never passed through. Epoch length and gap are pure functions of (CUT_SEED=20260813, epoch index); the per-cut hashes GAIN the epoch index and change in no other way. THE MAX GAP IS SET AGAINST THE PERSISTENCE, not by eye — and the silence is NOT the gap: the last birth of a sequence sits half a bin before it ends and the first birth of the next half a bin after it starts, so silence = gap + (1 + jitter)/rate = 0.40 + 0.0912 = 0.4912 rev against a 0.45 rev life, leaving the ring fully dark for at most 0.0412 rev = 0.0148 s = 0.44 of a 30 fps frame at the very worst draw the seed can produce. The first derivation of this bound read the silence as the gap alone, typed 0.52, and left a TWO-FRAME blackout that the falsification row measured off the rendered window. Undulation, not a strobe. ⚑ AND THE RATE IS THE RESTORED ONE (R-CPB-15): Matt pulled the density lever A2e's landing named, so this cadence aims its realized MEAN at the RATIFIED 11.0 cuts/rev (band +/-0.5) rather than at its own rate — the analytic mean above is 11.547 — and raising the rate shrank the blackout bound as a SIDE EFFECT, because narrower bins mean less slack at each end of a sequence.
